That's a bit of a cheekily narrow definition of explanation, isn't it? Explanations are always locally-, not globally-grounded. You can chase “Why?” down the stack of turtles forever

To offer Newton as an explanation for inertia is not an *illegitimate* explanation — it's merely so rote by this point in the sophistication of science that it's eminently clear to us that there IS a deeper level.

I've been watching more of your show lately — you're a really enjoyably sharp thinker!! Your erudition also stands out (you clearly know much more about physics than I do).

I'm a (sometime) philosopher of science, and so I appreciate the way you are basically democratizing philosophy of science for others even as I witness you struggling through its questions publicly primarily to satisfy your own curiosity (virtuous)

I'm curious the extent to which you conceive of *yourself* as a philosopher 👀 

Are you familiar with Derrida's Différance? It speaks to exactly this inescapability of meaning's deferral, and the lack of possibility for any ultimate ground… 

I don't think this means there isn't fruit in pursuing, say, theories of quantum gravity, but I think any true unifying theory must engage with such (ostensible?) constraints, and I would love to see how you handle such ideas
